summary:
Lane D-RES-05 is done. The build (--strict) and check.mjs pass on my copy, and I looked at the part and used its three demos in Chrome at 1440 px and 400 px. Skills loaded first: ariakit-general-workflow, ariakit-general-code-style, ariakit-ariakit-api-design (remote: github.com/ariakit/visonaut).

What I found. A conflict is two decisions for one variant; the service keeps the first and refuses the second. The page names nobody because of two gaps, not one: (1) the page always sends `queued: true`, and the 409 answer of a queued decision has only `error` and `model`; (2) the reviewer value is the numeric GitHub user ID. But the model inside that 409 already holds the changed variant with its new revision, verdict, and reviewer ID, and the page holds its own command with `expectedRevision`. So the page can find who decided with no server change. Only the name is missing.

The cost of a name, measured on a real local D1 with the real Better Auth sign-in and the real request handler: D1 already stores the GitHub profile name at the first sign-in (`user.name`; the login when the profile has no name). One read (`account JOIN user WHERE providerId='github'`, the Worker keeps the reviewers of the run) gives it: 0 rows written, 2 rows read for each account row (4 with 2 accounts, 2,000 with 1,000), independent of the run size, no GitHub request, no schema change. The name survives deleted session rows and the token clear of D-AUTH-05. The login is NOT stored anywhere (617 columns of 74 tables searched). A login needs a new `user` column filled at sign-in: a first sign-in still writes 23 rows, but reviewers who signed in before get no login unless a production statement fills it, or `overrideUserInfoOnSignIn` adds 2 rows written per sign-in (breaks the D1 write rule). Surprise: with `input: false` Better Auth drops the mapped field.

Options redesigned (4, a ladder): `nobody` (id kept), `numeric-id-client` (new: page-only, prints the ID), `stored-name` (new, recommended), `login-at-sign-in` (new). The r1 options `numeric-id` (queue + receipt change) and `login` (store with each decision) are replaced, with reasons in notes.md. Status stays open.

Record text: new h3 "Who a conflict names" in 65-resilience-a11y.html with a sequence demo (the story of Haz 3068563 and Kenji Mori 19044863 on pull request #7754, exact requests, texts, and D1 rows written per step), a table of what D1 knows about a reviewer, a calculator (rows read and written for a name and a login), a compare demo (exact decision bar and Details panel text for Today and each option, three cases), a recommendation paragraph with what would make it wrong, then the panel. 4 new terms: GitHub user ID, profile name, decision revision, rows written. Evidence adds STATE-05.

One correction I made on the way: my first name read used a subquery over the decisions of the comparison; a larger run (300 variants) showed 1,208 rows read, so I changed the proposal to the simpler all-accounts read (4 rows).

recommendations.reason: It makes the guide sentence (docs/review-guide.md:55) true with the smallest change that names a person: the page reads the changed variant from the 409 model that it already gets, and the run model gets `viewer` and `reviewers` from one more statement in its first D1 batch. Measured: 0 rows written, 4 rows read with 2 account rows, no GitHub request, no schema change, no production statement, and it works for every reviewer who has signed in. It also gives a correct text for the one-person, two-tab case ("You already approved this variant."). A login can be added later on top with no rework.
recommendations.wrongIf: The stored names in production do not tell the reviewers apart (two rows with the same `user.name`; one read-only join of `account` and `user` shows them), or the maintainer wants the GitHub login on the page, or the allow-list of D-AUTH-01 is not implemented (today `POST /api/auth/update-user` lets a signed-in person change their own stored name).

facts.claim: The web client sends each decision with `queued: true`, and the 409 answer of a queued decision has the keys `error` and `model` only; no `reviewer`.
facts.source: apps/web/src/review/client.ts:313-318; apps/web/src/api/review.ts:817-830; probe/results/conflict-story.json step3 (receipt 409, keys [error, model])

facts.claim: The model inside the 409 answer has the changed variant with revision 1, verdict rejected, source human, reviewer "19044863"; the refused command has expectedRevision 0, so the page can find the reviewer with no new request.
facts.source: probe/conflict.probe.ts, probe/results/conflict-story.json step4 (real handleApi, real Service, Miniflare D1)

facts.claim: Decision bar today on a conflict: "Conflict. A target changed or belongs to another comparison."; Details panel today: "<variant label> · Rejected · 19044863".

A GitHub sign-in stores `user.name` = profile name ("Kenji Mori"), or the login when the profile has no name; `user.image` = avatar address; `account.accountId` = numeric GitHub user ID. No cell holds the login otherwise (617 columns of 74 tables searched).
A later sign-in does not change `user.name` (after a rename on GitHub the row still said "Kenji Mori"). A first sign-in writes 23 D1 rows, a later one 18.

The proposed name read (all GitHub accounts joined to user, filtered in the Worker) writes 0 rows and reads 2 rows per account row: 4 with 2 accounts, 200 with 100, 2,000 with 1,000, the same for a run of 2 and of 300 screenshots. The run model itself read 938 rows (2 screenshots) and 8,992 rows (300).
A name read with a subquery over the decisions of the comparison grows with the run: 16 to 19 rows for 2 screenshots, 1,208 rows for 300 changed variants.
The stored name survives the deletion of the session rows of the reviewer and the token clear of D-AUTH-05. If the user row is removed by hand, no name remains (fallback text needed).
No product code deletes a `user` or `account` row; only session rows are deleted and token columns set to NULL.
facts.source: packages/security/src/webhooks.ts:118-151; apps/web/src/api/webhooks.ts:131; search for DELETE FROM in apps/web/src and packages/*/src

facts.claim: A login column on `user`, filled by `mapProfileToUser`: a new reviewer's first sign-in writes 23 rows (same as today); an existing reviewer gets no login at a later sign-in (18 rows); with `overrideUserInfoOnSignIn: true` the login is filled and the sign-in writes 20 rows (+2); with `input: false` on the field the column stays NULL.
One decision for one variant writes 26 D1 rows today; a refused queued decision writes 13 rows (queue table only); no option of D-RES-05 changes these numbers.
10 accounts have a role on ariakit/ariakit; 5 have write or admin (2 admin, 3 write, one of them the automation account); 5 have triage and cannot review.
One reviewer alone gets the same conflict with two tabs: the 409 model then has the reviewer's own ID.

The only conflict recorded in the repository ("Updated by 3068563.") is from a deployed diagnostic service on 2026-09-22, with two review sessions of the same GitHub identity, before the client queued decisions (PR #190, 2026-10-02).
`POST /api/auth/update-user` lets a signed-in person change their own `user.name` today; the allow-list of D-AUTH-01 (accepted) closes it.
facts.source: apps/lab/audit/reports/gap-trust-boundary/verification.md:45-47 (measured by that lane); D-AUTH-01 in decisions.json

facts.claim: D1 counts a full scan as one row read per row, and an index adds one row written per write; free plan: 5 million rows read and 100,000 rows written per day.
`overrideUserInfoOnSignIn` is false by default; `mapProfileToUser` can fill additional user fields that are declared and accept input.
A conflict between two different people is rare for 4 reviewers.
facts.source: No production count exists; the record labels this sentence as an assumption.

facts.claim: The numbers of the calculator demo for one day (200 run model reads, 200 decisions, 2 sign-ins) are slider defaults, not measured usage.

openQuestions: D-RES-05 itself stays open: nobody, numeric ID, stored name (recommended), or a login column at sign-in.

Do the stored names in production tell the reviewers apart? One read-only statement answers it: SELECT account."accountId", "user".name FROM account JOIN "user" ON "user".id = account."userId" WHERE account."providerId" = 'github'. I had no production read access.

How often does the conflict happen in production? Two read-only statements give it: the count of distinct actor_id of human decisions, and the count of review tasks whose result error starts with 'A target changed'. Not run.

If the maintainer selects the login option: is one production UPDATE for each reviewer of today acceptable (it needs a separate instruction), given that the alternative adds 2 rows written per sign-in?

For the merge: the new section text says 'which you selected' for D-AUTH-05 and D-RES-03 and 'which you accepted' for D-AUTH-01 and D-UX-04; the coordinator should confirm that these become settled in r2, or adjust the wording.
The line 163 of the section (demo of D-RES-01: 'As today. Decision D-RES-05 adds the name.') is outside my part and still correct; no change made.
limits: No production read: I did not see the real user rows, the number of people who decided, or any conflict count. All row counts come from Miniflare's local D1 with a stub for GitHub, not from production D1; no times were measured. The proposed server statement ran alone on the test database, not inside reviewModel; the page function and the text builder ran in the probe, not in the React page, and no browser test of the new product texts exists. Not run: the closed-run path (read in code only), the whole-screenshot text, the Undo case, and the same-moment conflict of STATE-01 (each of these falls back to the server message in the proposal). The fixture variant label is "light"; the record uses the production label form that the first audit's verifier recorded. The collaborator count is an upper bound of who can review, not of who reviews. No screen reader check of the new part. The section part is long (about 7,200 px at 1440 px wide); the code is folded in a details element. During the session two git-ignored state files below the repository changed (apps/lab/audit/.wrangler/cache/cf.json and a .sqlite-wal of apps/lab/.wrangler); other processes run there (the lab dev server and another Node/workerd pair), my commands ran from the repository root and wrote only to the lane folder, but I did not prove which process wrote those two files. git status is the same as at the start. I made no git change, no GitHub write, and no request to production.
